name: Quit smoking and vaping for breath

lead: Quitting smoking or vaping is discussed as a way to remove smoke odour from the breath and reduce damage to the gums.
Reference sources describe smoking as a major risk factor for gum disease, which is a recognised cause of bad breath, and say quitting improves gum health.

paras: Smoking is described as impairing immune response and wound healing in the gums and contributing to periodontal disease, whose bacteria produce odorous sulfur compounds. Stopping removes the smoke source and the associated risk factor.

No harms from the practice itself are reported in the sources consulted. Nicotine withdrawal is a general clinical consideration and cessation support is available through clinicians. No appearance-specific trials were found.

lead: Quitting smoking and vaping for breath and oral appearance refers to the practice of stopping tobacco and nicotine use in order to reduce smoke odour on the breath and to protect the gums. It is discussed in looksmaxxing and grooming circles as a low-cost lifestyle change, alongside oral hygiene and dental care.

Reference sources link smoking to periodontal (gum) disease, which is described as the second most common cause of oral malodour (bad breath) after bacterial coating on the tongue [1]. Smoking is also described as arguably the most important environmental risk factor for periodontitis, with smokers showing more bone loss, attachment loss and tooth loss than non-smokers [2]. The same sources state that quitting improves periodontal health [2].
No trials specific to appearance outcomes of quitting were identified for this article, and the evidence on vaping and gum health is not covered in the reference material consulted.
infobox: Reduce smoke odour on the breath; protect gum health

paras: The practice consists of stopping cigarette smoking or nicotine vaping. In appearance-focused communities it is framed as one of several mouth-related habits, together with brushing, tongue cleaning and professional dental care.

Wikipedia's article on halitosis states that most genuine cases originate in the mouth, with bacterial biofilm on the back of the tongue the leading cause, and that smoking is linked with periodontal disease, the second most common cause. It notes that not everyone with gum disease has bad breath [1].

The periodontal disease article describes smoking as a major environmental risk factor that impairs the immune response and wound healing, and states that quitting smoking enhances periodontal health [2]. The article does not give figures on the size or timing of improvement, and it does not discuss vaping [2].
